## 2026-08-12 — The saved-game restore path is now testable in ONE process, a save probe that does not pause first tests nothing, and `IsGameOver` was eliminated too early: `World.OutOfSync` is a second, independent caller of `EndGame`

> **[promoted — already landed]** (curation 2026-08-19). `architecture.md` §Saved games already carries every durable claim in this entry, re-read and confirmed at `de78a1ed`: the order-stream format, the accelerated fast-forward with the un-gated `world.TickRender` leftover, the necessarily-trailing `Pause` and the probe-that-looks-green pitfall, the single validating sync-hash comparison and the unrecoverable-pause chain, and the **enumerate-the-setters** lesson (the doc goes further than this entry — `World.EndGame()` has FOUR call sites, not two, the extra pair being Lua fatal-error handlers). The harness half (`run-test.sh` lock race, `debug.log` shelf life) is `WORKSPACE`/recipe material, not bank material. **One consequence of this entry IS now stale and has been corrected in this pass** — the doc's "restore is not reliably deterministic at real-match scale" line; see the greens listed on the 2026-08-16 entries.

Second half of the user-reported saved-game bug (`auto/saved-game-pause`; first half — the black viewport — merged at `1c80e279`). Headline: **the stuck pause did not reproduce.** The rest is the machinery that establishes that, plus one correction to a recorded negative result that would otherwise send the next reader the wrong way.

- **A saved-game restore can be driven end-to-end without touching the GUI, and it fits in one process.** Loading a save is not a main-menu-only operation: `GameSaveBrowserLogic.Load` is just `Game.CreateAndStartLocalServer(mapUid, [LoadGameSave(file), state Ready])`, and the in-game menu reaches the same code (`IngameMenuLogic.cs:428-445`). So a world trait can request a save, wait for `INotifyGameSaved`, and restart itself into the restore — the world is rebuilt from the same map, so the trait comes back and only needs a `static` field to know which life it is in. That is `GameSaveRoundTripProbe` (`engine/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/GameSaveRoundTripProbe.cs`) driving the `test-savegame-resume` scenario. **Nothing had ever exercised this path automatically before.**
- **PITFALL: a probe that calls `RequestGameSave` directly reproduces nothing, and looks green while doing it.** Saving is only reachable from the in-game menu, and opening that menu issues `SetPauseState(true)` (`MenuButtonsChromeLogic.cs:116-117`) — a *non-immediate* order, so `GameSave.DispatchOrders` records it (`GameSave.cs:209-211` skips only `0xFE` immediates). **Every real save's order stream therefore ends with a Pause, and the whole bug lives in what happens when that replays.** Two runs passed before this was noticed; the trace tell is `restore complete — paused=False`, i.e. the restored world never came back paused at all, so the pause round-trip under investigation was skipped end to end. The faithful shape is: pause, let the order settle a few frames, *then* request the save.
  - Corollary that bites immediately afterwards: once that stand-in pause lands, `World.Tick` stops ticking actors (`World.cs:494`) and **`ITick` never fires again** — but a real player saves from exactly that paused state. Anything the probe must do from there has to live in `ITickRender`, which `World.TickRender` runs regardless of pause (`World.cs:518-523`, "ignoring pause state"). Same reason the post-restore observation must be `ITickRender`: a probe for a stuck-pause bug must not be gated by the pause it is measuring.
- **Negative result (the actual finding).** With a `stable` bot opponent, a 900-tick recorded match and a genuine trailing Pause, the restore behaves exactly as designed: `GameLoaded` fires with `paused=True`, `LoadWidgetAtGameStart.cs:83-88` re-opens the options menu, and dismissing it via the menu's `RESUME` button (`IngameMenuLogic.cs:495-500` → `CloseMenu` → the `onExit` that restores `cachedPause`) leaves `paused=False` with the world ticking. The documented round-trip is not merely self-consistent on paper — it works.
- **`IsGameOver` was ruled out too early, and the gap matters.** The earlier elimination (`MissionObjectives.cs:174`'s predicate is unsatisfiable while the local player reads "Mission: In progress") is correct, but `MissionObjectives` is only **one of two** callers of `World.EndGame()`. The other is `World.OutOfSync()` (`World.cs:681-686`) — and it sits directly on the saved-game path, because the restore is validated by exactly one sync-hash comparison: `GameSave.ParseOrders` ends with `packetFn(LastSyncFrame, 0, lastSyncPacket)` (`GameSave.cs:262-263`, comment "Send sync hash to validate restore"), the client sends a real hash only once `NetFrameNumber >= GameSaveLastSyncFrame` and zeros before that (`OrderManager.cs:283-288`), and `ReceiveSync` calls `OutOfSync` on mismatch (`:174-181`). Failing that single check lands in `EndGame()` → `SetPauseState(true)` then `IsGameOver` latched (`World.cs:74-87`), after which `SetPauseState` early-returns (`:455`) and `UnitOrders` drops inbound unpause orders (`UnitOrders.cs:230-231`). **Unrecoverable pause, matching "the game seems ended, I cant unpause it" exactly.** Status: **CONFIRMED** by the River Zeta run below — this is the mechanism, not a hypothesis. *General lesson: "trait X cannot have set this flag" is not the same as "this flag cannot have been set" — enumerate the setters, not the story you started with. The original elimination was sound reasoning about the wrong caller, and it would have kept the real cause closed indefinitely.*
- **The obvious divergence trigger for that hypothesis does NOT exist in WW3MOD — checked, so nobody re-derives it.** The restore suppresses bot ticks (`ModularBot.cs:206`, `:304` — early-return while `IsLoadingGameSave`), which is only sound if a bot tick has no synced side effects. The natural offender is a `world.SharedRandom` draw, since `SharedRandom.Last` is summed straight into `World.SyncHash()` (`World.cs:564`): a draw that happened in the recorded match but not in the replay shifts the stream and changes the hash. There are only two draw sites under `Traits/BotModules/`, and **neither is live**: `ThreatMapManager.cs:71` is in `IWorldLoaded.WorldLoaded` (runs identically in both lives, not bot-gated), and `ScoutBotModule.cs:222-223` sits inside `FindRandomFarCell`, reached only when `threatMap == null` (`:173`) — but `ThreatMapManager` is registered on the world actor (`mods/ww3mod/rules/world.yaml:283`), so that branch is dead. The suppression is RNG-safe today. **Standing hazard worth naming:** any future `IBotTick` module that draws `SharedRandom` silently breaks saved-game restore, with no symptom until someone loads a save. **Since the divergence is now confirmed to be real, ruling this out matters: whatever diverges, it is NOT synced-RNG drift from the suppressed bot ticks.** Next places to look, in order — synced state mutated inside `ModularBot`'s own suppressed tick other than RNG; `IGameSaveTraitData` round-trips that do not restore a trait exactly (`World.cs:626-640` / `:471-483`); and any trait whose synced state depends on `ITickRender` or on real time rather than on `WorldTick`.
- **CONFIRMED at River Zeta scale: the restore fails its sync-hash check, and that is the stuck pause.** Same probe on the canonical 98×82 map, two bots (`@experimental` vs `@stable`), save at tick 3000. Verdict: `paused=True predictedpaused=True gameover=True worldtick=3003`. The trace shows the latch arriving *after* a clean restore — `restore complete — gameover=False … netframe=1007`, then `IsGameOver latched after restore — gameover=True … netframe=1008`. **Independent confirmation of the caller, not just the probe's own assertion:** the run wrote `syncreport-…-0.log` containing `Out of sync frame: 1004`, and `SyncReport.DumpSyncReport` has exactly ONE call site — `OrderManager.cs:90`, inside `OutOfSync(frame)`. So `OutOfSync` demonstrably fired, which rules out the `MissionObjectives` caller (it writes no sync report). Chain closed: divergence at the validation frame → `OutOfSync` → `World.OutOfSync()` → `EndGame()` → `SetPauseState(true)` + `IsGameOver`, after which the pause control is inert. **Both** River Zeta runs desynced (frames 1003 and 1004), so the earlier run whose verdict the lock race destroyed was the same fault — 2 for 2. The 900-tick arena passes, so this is scale/content dependent, which is exactly why the user hit it on a real match and the first test did not.
  - **NAMED (2026-08-12, instrumented run): the diverging field is `Detectable.visionDetectableConditionToken`, and it is a WW3MOD trait, not stock.** With `Test.ForceSyncReports` arming reports for the single-client case and the recording side dumped on the `GameSaved` acknowledgement, the two sides can be diffed directly. Frame 1002, **34,084 lines each, exactly 3 traits differ** — all `Detectable`, all the same field, each off by exactly one: `4692 e3.america USA-bot 144→143`, `4693 e2.america Russia-bot 42→41`, `4698 mt.america Russia-bot 41→40`. Everything else is identical **including `SharedRandom: 379693090 (#7958)` on both sides**, so RNG-stream drift is now ruled out by runtime evidence and not merely by the earlier static read.
  - **Why a condition token cannot survive a restore.** A token is an opaque allocation handle: `GrantCondition` hands out an increasing id, so its numeric value counts how many conditions that actor has ever been granted. `Detectable.DetectableVisionChanged` (`Detectable.cs:152-158`) revokes and re-grants on **every** visibility change, so the token advances once per change. Marking it `[Sync]` (`:149`) puts the *identity of the handle* into the sync hash rather than the gameplay state it stands for — so one missed visibility transition anywhere in the replay fails the restore's single validating comparison, even though nothing a player could observe differs. Off-by-exactly-one on all three actors means precisely one missed `DetectableVisionChanged` each, not accumulated drift.
  - **Ownership: WW3MOD.** `Detectable.cs` was added by `4eed77af` "Progressive fog (#5)", and its three token fields (`:150`, `:162`, `:193`) are the **only** `[Sync]`-marked condition tokens in the entire engine — no stock OpenRA trait syncs one. So this is not stock restore behaviour and is not upstream's to fix.
  - **Do not assume the fix is dropping `[Sync]`.** That would stop the restore failing, but if the underlying cause is a genuinely missed visibility transition then removing the sync only stops *detecting* a real divergence. The open question — and the right next step — is why the restored replay performs one fewer `DetectableVisionChanged` for those actors.
  - Still not established: whether the user's own human-vs-bot configuration diverges the same way. The caveat is now **sharper, not weaker** — the trait that diverges is a *visibility* trait, and the local client in this scenario is a spectator, so "does who-is-watching change this" is exactly the question a human-player configuration would answer. Not spent a run on it. What is established regardless: WW3MOD's saved-game restore is **not reliably deterministic at real-match scale**, and when it isn't, the failure is precisely the reported one.
  - Reproduce: `./tools/autotest/run-test.sh --speed 8 --timeout 900 --sync-reports test-savegame-resume-riverzeta`, then diff `syncdiag-recorded-frame<N>-0.log` against the `syncreport-*` the desync writes. Evidence for the run above is archived under `~/.ww3mod-tests/screenshots/260812_004914_test-savegame-resume-riverzeta/`.
- **HARNESS: `run-test.sh`'s stale-lock reclaim can destroy a live run's verdict, and with several workers active it will.** `mkdir "${LOCK_DIR}"` is the atomic acquire (`run-test.sh:317`) but the holder's pid is only written at `:333`. A second runner arriving in that window reads an **empty** pid, so the `[ -n "${_holder}" ] && kill -0 …` guard short-circuits false, the liveness check is skipped entirely, and it falls through to "Reclaiming stale lock" — `rm -rf`ing a live holder's lock. `:337`'s `rm -f "${RESULT_FILE}"` then deletes the running worker's verdict, because `RESULT_FILE` is one shared path across every concurrent worker. **The loss is unrecoverable and mis-signposted**: the engine has already printed `[TestMode] result written: <status>` and exited, while the victim's runner reports "No result file written … the test hung or was closed by hand", which points the reader at the game rather than at the race. Cost a granted single-shot run here. Fixed by treating an empty pid as *live* (bail) rather than dead — mid-acquisition is the opposite of stale. The file's own header already warned that concurrent runs "silently corrupt each other"; this is that hazard arriving via the reclaim path rather than the two-batch path it was written for. **The deeper defect is unfixed:** one shared `RESULT_FILE` means any lock slip is data loss, and a per-run result path would remove the class. *Corollary for anyone reading a verdict: `debug.log` is truncated by the next game launch, so with siblings active the trace behind a verdict has a shelf life of minutes — copy it before doing anything else.*
- **The multi-minute load: the fast-forward is already accelerated AND already skips drawing — with one un-gated leftover.** Accelerated: `Game.cs:1001-1005` drops `logicInterval` to 1 ms and `renderInterval` to 200 ms (5 FPS) for the duration, `OrderManager.SuggestedTimestep` returns 1 while `IsLoadingGameSave` (`:222-225`), and `Game.cs:1031` suppresses the force-one-render-per-logic-tick that otherwise caps sim throughput. Not drawing: `RenderTick` skips `Viewport.Tick`/`PrepareRenderables`, `worldRenderer.Draw()` and `DrawAnnotations()` while loading (`Game.cs:875`, `:888`, `:900`) — only the loading screen is drawn. **The leftover:** `world.TickRender(worldRenderer)` (`Game.cs:813-815`) has **no `IsLoadingGameSave` gate**, so it runs once per replayed logic tick, driving `ITickRender` across every actor plus `ScreenMap.TickRender()` — on a 20 000-tick fast-forward that is 20 000 full render-state passes whose output is never drawn. Unmeasured, and the only place free speed plausibly remains; everything else about the load is architectural (an order stream, not a snapshot, so the cost is genuinely N sim ticks). Note `logicInterval` here is a local in `Game.Run`, not `world.Timestep` — this path does not touch the mutable-vs-invariant timestep trap at `1abb62e1`.
## 2026-08-12 — Pausing `Mobile` is the engine's "halt this order and resume it later" primitive; and a matched pair green on both sides still did not protect a third doctrine

> **[promoted in part]** → `conventions.md` §Engine behaviors that surprise (curation 2026-08-19, verified against `de78a1ed`). Both engine claims re-verified: `Move.Tick` returns **false** (not "ends") while `mobile.IsTraitPaused` (`Move/Move.cs:167`), `IsCanceling` is tested first at `:160` so a paused unit is still cancellable, and `MobileInfo : PausableConditionalTraitInfo` (`Mobile.cs:26`) makes it available on any actor. The `PauseOnCondition`-replaces-rather-than-merges trap was banked in its **general** form — a condition expression is a single field, so restating it on a child replaces the inherited one — since it applies to every such field, not just this trait; `^Vehicle` `:38` vs TRUK `:564` remain the worked example and the in-file comment at `:561-563` is still there. **Rejected from this entry**: the free-stance census for TRUK and the `SupplyInit` staging recipe (both situational to that branch), and the matched-pair/committed-errand lessons, which are already covered by `AUTOTEST.md`'s regression guidance and `supply-route.md`'s commitment section.

From `auto/truck-doctrine` (supply trucks: collect from the ground, halt to serve, break off when dry).

- **`Move.Tick` returns `false` while `mobile.IsTraitPaused` — it does NOT end the activity** (`Move.cs:168`). So granting a `Mobile.PauseOnCondition` condition stops a unit *mid-order* and revoking it resumes the same activity, with no re-issue and no path re-plan. That is the whole implementation of "stop for this, then carry on where you were going"; cancelling and re-queuing was the obvious alternative and is strictly worse, because the order that was interrupted is exactly the thing that has to survive. `MobileInfo` is a `PausableConditionalTraitInfo`, so this is available on any actor. Note `Move.Tick` checks `IsCanceling` *before* the pause check, so a paused unit can still be cancelled — a break-off does not have to un-pause first.
- **`PauseOnCondition` is a single field, so naming it on a child actor REPLACES the inherited expression rather than adding to it.** `^Vehicle` carries `PauseOnCondition: !(!empdisable && !being-captured)` (`vehicles.yaml:38`); a bare `PauseOnCondition: my-condition` on TRUK would silently let an EMP'd or mid-capture truck drive away. The inherited terms have to be restated. General MiniYaml point, easy to miss because the *trait* merges per-field while the *expression* does not.
- **The free-stance census for an unarmed support vehicle, done and worth reusing.** `ResupplyBehavior` is fully occupied on TRUK (all three values live, `Evacuate` its shipped default for human and AI). `UnitStance` is free but MEANINGLESS — TRUK declares no armament and `^Vehicle` does not inherit `^Combatant`, so a fire stance on it is not merely unread, a player cannot reason about it. `EngagementStance.HoldPosition` is the genuinely free value, and it is also the right *meaning*: `ControlAllUnitsManager.cs:56-59` already treats HoldPosition as "this unit stays under player control", i.e. "does what I told it and nothing else". **When looking for a free stance axis, check whether the value already carries a compatible meaning elsewhere — a free slot that means the wrong thing is worse than no slot.**
- **A `SupplyProvider` actor placed the ordinary way always spawns FULL** (`currentSupply` seeds from `TotalSupply`), so any scenario needing headroom must stage it with the `SupplyInit` the constructor reads: `Supply: 100` under the actor in `map.yaml`. Trait-scoped inits do load from map yaml — `ActorReference.LoadInit` finds `<Name>Init` by reflection and calls `Initialize(MiniYaml)`, bypassing the constructor.
- **THE EXPENSIVE LESSON: a behaviour verified by a matched pair on its own axis still broke a third scenario testing a doctrine it had no obvious connection to.** The serving halt shipped with both sides of its stance pinned and green (`test-truck-halts-to-serve` / `test-truck-holdposition-drives-past`), and broke the danger-mode drop-and-leave: a truck sent to unload NEAR a platoon halted to serve that platoon from its aura, never reached the drop cell, never placed a crate, and sat in the danger the errand was routing it out of. **What makes this the dangerous kind: the platoon still ended up resupplied**, so every visible outcome looked correct and only the shipped scenario's crate assertion caught it. `AUTOTEST.md`'s "re-run the scenario you were NOT working on" is what found it, and the reusable form is stronger than the existing wording: *a new behaviour that can fire during someone else's errand must be regression-checked against that errand, even when the two share no code and no axis.* Concretely, the question to ask is "what else moves this unit, and would stopping it there be wrong?"
- **The fix generalises into a rule worth keeping: a COMMITTED ERRAND needs a recognisable TYPE.** Three separate mechanisms on this branch all had to ask "what is this move FOR" — the halt, the dry break-off, and the restocking state. None could, because every errand was a bare `MoveTo` with a `CallFunc` queued behind it, which is indistinguishable from a player's move order. Giving each errand one named activity made all three answerable from one queue walk (`SupplyProvider.OnSupplyErrand`), and simultaneously fixed the latch that a bool-alongside-the-queue had caused. **A flag that records "an activity is in flight" must be cleared when the activity ENDS, not when it SUCCEEDS** — in an RTS cancellation is the common ending — and the way to make that unfalsifiable is to not have the flag: derive the state from the queue, which is what cancellation edits. Same technique as `AmmoPool.IsSeekingRearm`, and the walk must cover `NextActivity` and not just the head, because `QueueActivity(false, …)` *cancels* the current activity rather than removing it and the new one sits behind the corpse.

## 2026-08-11 — "Can this unit shoot?" has three different answers in this codebase, and picking the wrong grain is how the out-of-ammo move wedge survived its own fix

> **[promoted: → economy.md §"Can this unit shoot?" has THREE different answers, which REPLACES the coarser `CannotFight`-is-the-right-predicate paragraph promoted earlier today — this entry is the sharper version and the taxonomy is now a table. Re-verified: the `^E3` case exactly (`primary` DMR 100 rounds + `secondary` RPG 1 round, `infantry.yaml:1209-1245`; `RPG` declares `InvalidTargets: Infantry`, `weapons-ballistics.yaml:302`; both `ReloadAmmoPool`s gated `replenish-soldiers`), `Armament.CanFire`'s transient states (`Armament.cs:327`), and `CannotFight`'s aircraft carve-out (`AmmoPool.cs:216`). **Its one factual slip is inherited from the engine, and I corrected the engine.** The entry repeats `AmmoPool.cs:210-214`'s example that `PauseOnCondition` "also carries garrisoned-at-port" — no `Armament` in this mod carries it (it is on `Mobile` and `AttackFrontal` only), the same wrong counterexample flagged in the 2026-08-10 attack-activities entry. The caveat itself stands on `suppressed >= 10` / `empdisable` / `heavy-damage-attained` / `inwater`, which ARE real armament pause terms; the doc-comment has been rewritten to say so. The entry's own best insight — **the caveat attaches to the QUESTION, not to the predicate** — is banked.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ dc8e0abf).

Found finishing the out-of-ammo stall (`auto/ooa-rifleman`, second half of `auto/ooa-wedge`). The first fix gated the
move interrupt on `AmmoPool.CannotFight` and was correct — but it answered a *coarser* question than the one being
asked, and the bug survived intact for the mod's most common unit. The three grains, and when each is right:

- **Per-ACTOR — `AmmoPool.CannotFight(self)`.** "Nothing left to shoot with, anywhere." Requires EVERY pool empty.
  Right for the resupply dispatch (send this man to a truck?) and for cheap early-outs. **Wrong whenever the question
  is about a specific target**, because a unit can be unable to engage what is in front of it while a pool it cannot
  use here is still loaded.
- **Per-ARMAMENT, per-TARGET — `ChooseArmamentsForTarget(t, force)` plus `!a.IsTraitPaused`.** "Is there a weapon that
  is both legal against THIS target and able to fire?" `ChooseArmamentsForTarget` supplies the first half and
  deliberately not the second (it filters `IsTraitDisabled`, and an empty armament is *paused*).
- **Per-ARMAMENT firing gate — `Armament.CanFire` (`Armament.cs:327`).** Adds `IsReloading || IsWaitingBurst ||
  IsAiming`. Those are transient per-shot states; a decision about whether to stop moving must NOT read them, or a
  unit declines to engage purely because it is between bursts.

**The case that makes this concrete, and it is not exotic.** `^E3`, the standard rifleman, carries a DMR
(`primary-ammo`) and an RPG (`secondary-ammo`) whose weapon declares `InvalidTargets: Infantry`. After any
infantry-vs-infantry firefight the DMR is spent and the RPG is still loaded — there was never a legal target for it.
So against infantry his only offered armament is one he cannot fire, while `CannotFight` is false because a pool is
loaded. Both his `ReloadAmmoPool`s are gated `RequiresCondition: replenish-soldiers`, so it does not heal.
**Generalisation worth keeping: a multi-pool unit whose weapons have disjoint `ValidTargets` will routinely sit at
"empty for the enemy in front of me, loaded overall".** Any per-actor ammo predicate is blind to exactly that state.

**`IsTraitPaused` is the honest per-armament test, and its recorded caveat does not apply to every question.**
`AmmoPool.cs:210-214` warns against it as a `CannotFight` substitute because `PauseOnCondition` also carries things
like `garrisoned-at-port` — a garrisoned man with a full magazine must not be sent to resupply. But for "should I
stop walking to aim this?", pause-for-any-reason is exactly right, and it also picks up `suppressed >= 10`,
`empdisable` and `heavy-damage-attained` (all real `PauseOnCondition` terms in this mod's YAML), each of which wedges
a move by the identical route. **The caveat attaches to the QUESTION, not to the predicate** — a warning recorded
against one call site should not be read as a global prohibition.

**Where NOT to fix it: the shared method.** `ChooseArmamentsForTarget` has nine callers and its `// FF TODO Check
ammo?` comment reads like an invitation, but `AttackBase.AbandonWhenArmamentsPaused` was added *specifically* because
"every armament paused" must not end an attack by default ("holding aim through a brief pause is the wanted
behaviour"). Filtering paused armaments inside the shared method would silently flip that opt-in field on for every
unit in the game and strip the attack cursor off any momentarily-paused unit. **A standing TODO is not evidence that
the change is safe where it sits** — check whether a later opt-in was built precisely to avoid making it there.

## 2026-08-11 — `Game.RunAfterTick` runs INSIDE synced code, so the "click this button for the screenshot driver" idiom CTDs on any UI action that touches the order generator

> **[promoted: → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise. Re-verified exactly: `RunAfterTick` queues onto `delayedActions` (`Game.cs:735`), drained by `PerformDelayedActions()` on the FIRST line of `LogicTick()` (`:822-824`) — a synced context; `World.OrderGenerator`'s setter asserts unsynced with that verbatim message (`World.cs:168`), reached via `CancelInputMode()` (`:178`); the fix wrapper is `Sync.RunUnsynced(World, Action)` (`Sync.cs:165`). The load-bearing half is the ASYMMETRY — the real `OnClick` never trips it because input handling is already unsynced, so the button works for a human and explodes for the driver. The black-PNG size tell was banked with it. Minor drift: `AssertUnsynced` is `Sync.cs:205`, not `:208`.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ dc8e0abf).

Hit while adding `Test.OpenIngameInfoPanel` (the debug-panel twin of `Test.OpenSkirmishLobby`). The new hook copied the established idiom verbatim — `if (TestMode.IsActive && …) Game.RunAfterTick(<do the thing the button does>)` (`MainMenuLogic.cs:542-543`) — and crashed to desktop the moment the match loaded.

- **The trap.** `RunAfterTick` queues onto the `ActionQueue` drained by `Game.PerformDelayedActions()` **from inside `Game.LogicTick()`** (`Game.cs:824`, `:843`), which is synced. `MenuButtonsChromeLogic.OpenMenuPanel` calls `World.CancelInputMode()` → `World.OrderGenerator` setter → `Sync.AssertUnsynced` (`World.cs:168`, `:178`; `Sync.cs:208`) ⇒ `InvalidOperationException: The current order generator may not be changed from synced code`. The **real** `OnClick` never trips this because input handling is already an unsynced context — so the button works for a human and explodes for the driver, which is exactly the asymmetry that makes this easy to ship.
- **Why `Test.OpenSkirmishLobby` got away with it.** Its action (`StartSkirmishGame`) runs at the **main menu**, where there is no `World` and nothing asserts sync at all. So the existing idiom is only safe *pre-match*; copying it into a hook that fires **in-match** is where it breaks. Any future `Test.Open*` hook that drives in-game UI inherits this.
- **The fix is one wrapper:** `Game.RunAfterTick(() => Sync.RunUnsynced(world, () => …))` (`Sync.cs:165`). Keep `RunAfterTick` — deferring past construction is still needed — and add `RunUnsynced` for the synced-frame problem; they solve different things and you need both.
- **Diagnostic note for screenshot drivers: a crash still produces a PNG, and it is BLACK.** The capture command was consumed after the CTD, so `manifest.json` gained a normal-looking entry pointing at a 34 KB all-black image (a healthy full-screen capture here is ~1.1 MB). **File size is the cheap tell** — a screenshot driver that only checks "did the PNG appear" reports success on a crashed game. Check the log for `Exception of type` before trusting a capture.
- **Also: `screenshot.sh --wait` matches the label case-sensitively but the engine lowercases it** when sanitizing the filename (`SCREENSHOT.md`: "labels are lowercased"). A mixed-case label like `debug-presets-AFTER-…` therefore times out even though the capture succeeded and is sitting on disk. Use a lowercase label with `--wait`, or write the command file directly and poll the directory.

## 2026-08-11 — A duplicate trait key inside ONE actor resolves LAST-value-wins at the FIRST key's position; and `--resolved-rules` makes "which value wins" a build-only question, plus a byte-exact proof of behaviour-neutrality for any YAML refactor

> **[promoted: → conventions.md §A duplicate trait key inside ONE actor. Re-verified at source: `MergeIntoResolved` (`MiniYaml.cs:427-447`) locates the earlier node's index (`:430-435`) and writes the merged value back at that index (`:444`) — survivor keeps the FIRST position, takes the LAST values, merged per field. `MergeSelfPartial` (`:497`) is confirmed a different, top-level-only function. `--resolved-rules` exists (`UtilityCommands/OutputResolvedRulesCommand.cs`). **And the account checks out end to end:** `tunguska` now carries a single `Health:` block reading `HP: 8000` (`vehicles-russia.yaml`) — the value the engine was already fielding — so the de-dup landed and preserved behaviour exactly as the entry claims. The de-dup corollary (deleting the second block while keeping the first block's values is the one option that CHANGES behaviour, and the one that looks most obviously correct) is the half most worth having.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ dc8e0abf).

Found while de-duplicating `tunguska`'s two `Health:` blocks (`WORKSPACE/balance/001-tunguska-duplicate-health.md`). That doc asserted "static analysis cannot determine the engine's duplicate-key resolution with certainty; a combat-sim rules dump (once utility runs are granted) confirms the effective value" — **both halves are wrong**, and the correction is cheap and reusable.

- **The resolution rule, exactly.** Two same-named trait nodes inside a single actor do NOT produce two traits and do NOT throw. `ResolveInherits` walks the actor's children and hands each to `MergeIntoResolved` (`engine/OpenRA.Game/MiniYaml.cs:449-491`, `:427-447`), which on a repeat key looks up the earlier node's index and writes `existingNodes[existingNodeIndex] = existingNode.WithValue(MergePartial(existingNode.Value, overrideNode.Value))`. So the survivor **keeps the FIRST occurrence's position in the node list but takes the LAST occurrence's field values** — and field-level merge is per-key, so a later block that sets only *some* fields overrides only those and inherits the rest from the earlier block. The familiar `MergeSelfPartial` (`:497-518`) is a *different* function that only de-dupes **top-level** keys per source; it never sees this case. Concretely: `tunguska` declared `HP: 14000` then `HP: 8000` thirteen lines later, and the actor fields **8000**.
- **The blast radius is bigger than a wrong number: the dead block is invisible to every reader AND to `make test`.** The YAML lint does not flag duplicate child keys, so an actor can carry a plausible-looking stat that the engine has never used, for as long as nobody dumps it. Any balance pass that reads the file top-down and stops at the first `Health:` tunes a value with no effect.
- **`./utility.sh --resolved-rules <actor>` answers it in one command, with no game run and no autotest budget.** It needs only a successful build, prints the fully merged/inherited node list for the actor, and is not gated by the "no autonomous multi-test runs" rule because it launches no match. Actor names are case-sensitive here even though actor *lookup* elsewhere is not — use the lowercase ruleset key (`tunguska`, not `Tunguska`).
- **The reusable technique — diff the resolved dump around the edit.** For any "clean up this YAML without changing behaviour" task, capture `--resolved-rules <actor>` before and after and `diff` them. Identical output is a byte-exact proof of behaviour-neutrality across the *whole* actor — inheritance, `-Removals`, faction variants and all — which is far stronger than eyeballing the edited lines, and it catches the classic blank-line/adjacent-entry merge accident (`CLAUDE.md` hard rule) as a side effect. Used here to prove the Tunguska dedup changed nothing.
- **Corollary for de-duplicating: preserving the resolved value is NOT the same as keeping the block you'd expect.** Because the survivor sits at the *first* position but carries the *last* values, the behaviour-neutral edit is "keep the earlier block's slot, write the later block's values into it, delete the later block" — deleting the *first* block instead also preserves behaviour but silently relocates the trait in the file. Deleting the *second* block while keeping the first block's values is the one option that **changes** behaviour, and it is the one that looks most obviously correct.
## 2026-08-11 — Saved games are a REPLAY, not a snapshot: load time is proportional to match length, and the restored world renders all-black because `MenuPaletteEffect` is never faded in

> **[promoted (partial): → architecture.md §Saved games: an order stream, not a snapshot (new) and §All bot orders funnel through `ModularBot.QueueOrder` (the desync invariant). Re-verified exactly: the `.orasav` format comment (`GameSave.cs:273-286`), `GameSaveLoadingPercentage` (`World.cs:121`), the trailing-Pause round-trip, and the palette-effect fingerprint — that last one is the durable half of the black-viewport finding and outlives the bug, which was fixed at `1c80e279`. **ONE CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED, and the day's experimental work is what overturned it.** The bullet "`IsGameOver` is NOT the cause of the stuck pause (ruled out; negative result worth recording)" is WRONG. The reasoning about `MissionObjectives` was sound but the scope was not: `World.EndGame()` has **four** call sites — `MissionObjectives.cs:180`, `World.OutOfSync` (`World.cs:694`), and two Lua fatal-error handlers (`ScriptContext.cs:274`, `:296`). The restore's single validating sync-hash comparison fails, lands in `OutOfSync` → `EndGame()`, and latches `IsGameOver` — which IS the reported stuck pause, CONFIRMED at River Zeta scale. The 08-12 entries above supersede this bullet and the entry's closing "not yet explained" caveat. There is now a PITFALL at `World.cs:686`. **ONE CLAIM IS TOO STRONG:** "the fast-forward is already about as fast as this design allows … the only lever left is not running them" — `world.TickRender` (`Game.cs:813-815`) is gated only on `LocalFrameNumber > 0`, NOT on `IsLoadingGameSave`, so it runs a full render-state pass per replayed tick for output that is never drawn. Unmeasured, and the one remaining lever. **Rejected: narrow** — the in-flight leak hunt (08-12 chain: onset frames, named actors, the `Detectable` `[Sync]` hypothesis that VERIFIED RED, the located-but-unnamed second leak) is a live investigation and belongs with its branch, not in a doc trusted without re-verification. NOTE for `WORKSPACE/plans/260812_multiplayer_continuity.md`: its §3 already encodes the corrected picture (replay-not-snapshot, and "ours provably did not" reproduce), so the plan does NOT rest on the expired bullet; but its line 40 "not optimisable — it is the architecture" inherits the too-strong claim above, and its open question about `e1bbf244` is answered NEGATIVE by the VERIFIED RED entry.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ dc8e0abf).

Static read at `main @ d6d7244b`, prompted by the first user test of load-game (`Conquest: River Zeta WW3`, ~5 min to load, black viewport, stuck paused). **Nobody had exercised this path before.**

- **`.orasav` stores an order stream, not world state.** The file format comment is explicit (`engine/OpenRA.Game/Network/GameSave.cs:273-286`): "List of orders in network frame format", then lobby metadata, then a small custom-trait blob. `DispatchOrders` (`:191-234`) appends every non-immediate order as the match runs; `ParseOrders` (`:236-264`) pushes the whole stream back from frame 0 and finishes with the recorded sync hash to validate the restore. **There is no snapshot of actors, resources, or map state anywhere in the format.** Loading therefore re-simulates the entire match from tick 0, so *load time scales with how long the saved match ran* — a five-minute load of a long game is the architecture working as designed, not a performance bug. Micro-optimisation cannot fix this; only a real snapshot mechanism, or an honest ETA, would.
- **The fast-forward is already about as fast as this design allows.** `Game.cs:1001-1005` drops `logicInterval` to 1 ms and caps rendering at 5 FPS (`renderInterval = 200`) for the duration, and `OrderManager.SuggestedTimestep` returns 1 while `World.IsLoadingGameSave` (`OrderManager.cs:209-211`). So rendering is *not* the waste — the cost is genuinely N sim ticks, and the only lever left is not running them. Note `Game.cs:1031` also suppresses the force-render-per-tick that normally caps sim throughput, i.e. the same trick `Test.SpeedMultiplier` relies on is already applied here.
- **`World.GameSaveLoadingPercentage` is ticks-replayed, so a real ETA is already available for free.** `World.cs:121` is `NetFrameNumber * 100 / GameSaveLastFrame` — both terms are known up front, and progress is near-linear in ticks, so elapsed/percent extrapolates directly. The progress bar currently shows the fraction but no time estimate.
- **THE BLACK VIEWPORT: `MenuPaletteEffect` starts at `Black` and, on the saved-game path, nothing ever fades it back.** The trait initialises `from = to = EffectType.Black` (`MenuPaletteEffect.cs:42-43`). `IWorldLoaded.WorldLoaded` deliberately *skips* the fade-in while `IsLoadingGameSave` (`:118`), deferring to `INotifyGameLoaded.GameLoaded` — which fades **only `if (world.IsReplay)`** (`:127`). A saved game is not a replay, so the branch never fires. The compensating mechanism named in the HACK comment ("let the menu opening trigger the fade") does not exist for this trait: `IngameMenuLogic` resolves `TraitOrDefault<MenuPostProcessEffect>()` (`IngameMenuLogic.cs:187`) — **a different trait** — so `mpe` is null and both `mpe?.Fade(...)` at `:188` and `CloseMenu`'s at `:316` are silent no-ops. WW3MOD registers `MenuPaletteEffect` (`mods/ww3mod/rules/palettes.yaml:144`), so it takes the broken branch. `AdjustPalette` then blacks every world palette for the rest of the session (`:92-112`).
- **Why the minimap and sidebar survive while the world does not — and why this signature is diagnostic.** `MenuPaletteEffect` is an `IPaletteModifier`: it only reaches *palettised* rendering, i.e. terrain and actor sprites. Chrome, the radar minimap texture, and world annotations (health bars, selection/ownership decorations) are drawn RGBA and bypass palettes entirely. **So "black terrain + correct minimap + health bars floating on black" is the fingerprint of a palette-effect fault, not of a failed map parse or a broken terrain renderer** — the map data is provably fine precisely *because* the minimap drew it.
- **`IsGameOver` is NOT the cause of the stuck pause (ruled out; negative result worth recording).** The tempting story is `World.EndGame()` (`World.cs:74-87`), which pauses and then latches `IsGameOver`, after which every `SetPauseState` early-returns (`:453-455`) and `UnitOrders` drops incoming unpause orders (`UnitOrders.cs:230-231`) — a genuinely unrecoverable pause that would match "the game seems ended, I cant unpause it" exactly. But it cannot have fired here: the reported "Mission: In progress" is bound to `player.WinState == WinState.Undefined` (`GameInfoObjectivesLogic.cs:57-58`), and `CheckIfGameIsOver` requires `Players.All(p => p.NonCombatant || p.WinState != Undefined || !p.HasObjectives)` (`MissionObjectives.cs:174`). `ConquestVictoryConditions.Tick` adds the primary objective on the owner's first tick (`:66-67`), which sets `HasObjectives = true` via `MissionObjectives.cs:266`, so a live local player with an undefined win state falsifies the predicate. **Careful: the objectives panel does not guard on objective count** (`GameInfoObjectivesLogic.cs:40-51` only early-returns on a null player or null trait), so "In progress" alone does not prove objectives exist — the `ConquestVictoryConditions` first-tick add is what closes it.
- **Every save necessarily records a trailing `Pause` order, which is why the restore deliberately re-opens the options menu.** Saving is only reachable from the in-game menu, and `MenuButtonsChromeLogic.OpenMenuPanel` issues `SetPauseState(true)` on the way in (`:97-98`) — a non-immediate order, so `GameSave.DispatchOrders` records it (`GameSave.cs:209-211` only skips `0xFE` immediates). The restore therefore always ends paused, and `LoadWidgetAtGameStart.GameLoaded` compensates by issuing `SetPauseState(false)` and re-clicking the options button (`:83-88`) to reproduce the player's saved context. `OpenMenuPanel` captures `cachedPause = world.PredictedPaused` (`:87`) and restores it on exit (`:113-114`). **This round-trip is self-consistent on paper** — which is exactly why the observed stuck pause is not yet explained, and why it should be re-tested after the black-viewport fix before being treated as a separate defect.
## 2026-08-11 — There is NO free modifier on a build-menu icon: every LMB gesture queues production, ww3mod infantry render no selection box at all, and selection classes are shared across factions

> **[promoted (partial): → architecture.md §Widget / chrome authoring gotchas — the selection-invisibility half, which is the durable and expensive one. Re-verified: `^Infantry` `SelectionDecorations: ShowNever: true` (`infantry.yaml:55`, the only one in the mod) against `SelectionDecorationsBase.cs:109` `if (selected && !Info.ShowNever)`; and the vehicle surprise at `:129`, `renderDecorations = selected ? selectedDecorations : decorations` — the UNSELECTED path draws the brackets, so the bracket is not a selection indicator. `Test.GetSelectedCount`/`GetSelectedCountOfType` confirmed at `TestGlobal.cs:187`/`:194`. **Rejected: the sidebar-gesture half** (Ctrl/Alt orthogonality, which combination is cheapest to displace) is a design rationale for one shipped gesture, not a system fact — it belongs with `auto/select-by-type`. The selection-class note (match on selection class, not actor name, or veterans are silently missed) is genuinely useful but is a property of the YAML anyone can grep; not banked.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ dc8e0abf).

Found at `main @ d6d7244b` building Ctrl+Alt+LMB select-by-type (branch `auto/select-by-type`). Four findings, each of which changes what a future UI change on the sidebar can assume.

- **Ctrl+Alt+LMB on a build-menu icon was NOT free, and neither is any other modifier combination.** `ProductionPaletteWidget.HandleLeftClick` reads Ctrl and Alt as two *independent orthogonal flags*, not as a combined tier: `queued = !Ctrl` (`:378`, priority-insert at the head of the queue) and `auto = Alt` (`:379`, `Infinite`/auto-rebuild). So Ctrl+Alt+LMB already meant "insert at the front AND repeat forever". Because the flags are orthogonal, **there is no free *combination* — only a free *modifier*** (`Meta`), and even a bare unmodified LMB queues a unit, so *every* gesture on an icon already does something. Any new sidebar gesture must therefore *displace* an existing one; the question is only which loss is cheapest, not which slot is empty. The one taken here (Ctrl+Alt) is the cheapest because both flags stay individually reachable as Ctrl+click and Alt+click, and `queued=false` is a no-op whenever the queue is empty — the common case.
- **Ctrl+Alt is *also* the mod's fourth keyboard-hotkey tier, but that is a different input surface and does not collide.** `engine/mods/common/hotkeys/game.yaml:117-157` binds ten stance/cohesion/resupply hotkeys as `<key> Ctrl, Alt`. Those are `HandleKeyPress` bindings; the sidebar gesture is `HandleMouseInput`. Separately, `SelectionPriorityMath.Suppressed` deliberately returns false when *both* Ctrl and Alt are held (`SelectionPriorityMathTest.cs:66-67`), so Ctrl+Alt is already the neutral "no priority filtering" state in world selection — consistent with using it for a gesture that wants the raw set.
- **You cannot tell a selected unit from an unselected one by looking at it, and this is NOT limited to infantry — a screenshot can never demonstrate a selection in this mod.** Two separate mechanisms, established by measurement rather than by reading:
  - Infantry are explicit: `mods/ww3mod/rules/ingame/infantry.yaml:54-55` sets `SelectionDecorations: ShowNever: true` on `^Infantry`, and `SelectionDecorationsBase.cs:109` is literally `if (selected && !Info.ShowNever)`, so the selection box is never drawn for any infantry. This is the only `ShowNever` in the mod.
  - **Vehicles are the surprise.** Own vehicles render white corner brackets and pips *whether or not they are selected*, so the bracket reads as a selection box but is not one. Measured by full-frame pixel diff of the before/after captures in `test-select-by-type`: selecting four Bradleys changed **zero pixels** anywhere on those units, and the same held for four Abrams in the previous run — in both runs the *only* changed pixels in the whole world area were a 51×31 px block at the Supply Route flag (its idle animation, 1104 px, identical in both runs). Cross-checked against `test-screenshot-smoke`, whose selected M109 also shows brackets. So the bracket is drawn on the unselected path (`renderDecorations = selected ? selectedDecorations : decorations`, `:129`) and selection adds nothing on top.
  - What *does* change visibly is UI chrome, not the units: the bottom command bar (~12.5k px) and the text-notification feed. **Consequence: verify selection from game state, never from a capture.** `Test.GetSelectedCount()` / `Test.GetSelectedCountOfType(type)` exist for exactly this. Two full scenario rewrites (infantry → Abrams → Bradley) were burned chasing a visible selection box that does not exist for any unit type.
- **Selection classes are shared across factions for equivalent roles, and veteran variants inherit the base class.** `Class: MBT` is on abrams / t90 / the Ukraine MBT (`vehicles-america.yaml:549`, `vehicles-russia.yaml:382`, `vehicles-ukraine.yaml:84`); `ARTILLERY` and `MLRS` are each shared across two factions; `Pilot` across five actors. Veterans inherit their base's class (`^E3` sets `Class: E3`, and `E3R1.america` inherits it) while carrying `-Buildable`, so they have no icon of their own. **So select-by-type must match on selection class, not on actor name**: name-matching would silently miss every veteran, and the cross-faction sharing is inert because selection is already owner-filtered (`GetPlayersToIncludeInSelection`). `Selectable` falls back to the lowercased actor name when `Class` is unset (`Selectable.cs:49`), which is why an icon name and a class name are interchangeable for the ~90% of actors that set neither.
## 2026-08-11 — The out-of-ammo freeze was in the MOVE wrapper, not the attack path: `SmartMoveActivity` interrupts on a weapon it never checks the ammo of, and "Move" is wrapped while "ForceMove" is not

> **[promoted (partial): → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise — the **`Move` vs `ForceMove` fork detail**, which is the durable half and was not in the bank. Re-verified verbatim: two order strings at `Mobile.cs:1002`, `"Move"` queued through `WrapMove(...)` at `:1021`, `"ForceMove"` queued bare at `:1031-1033` with the in-code comment *"Force-move bypasses WrapMove — pure movement, no SmartMove wrapping"* (plus `NoReverse = true`, which the entry does not mention). Banked as a **diagnostic signature**: "ignores Move, obeys Force-Move" localises a fault to a move wrapper rather than to the pathfinder, locomotor or order — and an errand issued via `Mobile.MoveWithinRange` is wrapped too, which is why a target line can be drawn by an activity whose movement never runs. **Rejected: narrow** — the specific wedge is fixed, and the `ChooseArmamentsForTarget` half is already covered better by the three-grain table now in economy.md. The containment argument is worth restating where it lands though: reusing `AmmoPool.CannotFight` makes the set of units the resupply layer sends away exactly the set `SmartMoveActivity` refuses to pin, so a unit cannot be both "too dry to interrupt" and "not dry enough to send".]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ dc8e0abf).

Reported from live play: a dry unit gets its resupply order (green line to the truck is drawn) but never travels, ignores plain Move orders, and only obeys Force-Move. Fixed on `auto/ooa-wedge`; RED→GREEN observed on two scenarios, with the unchanged branch pinned by a third.

- **The Move/Force-Move asymmetry is the whole diagnosis, and it is a WW3MOD-only fork detail.** Stock OpenRA emits one `"Move"` order for both; this fork emits two order strings (`Mobile.cs:1002`), and `ResolveOrder` treats them differently on purpose: `"Move"` is wrapped by every `IWrapMove` trait (`Mobile.cs:1021`), `"ForceMove"` **bypasses the wrappers entirely** (`:1032`, "pure movement, no SmartMove wrapping"). `^Infantry` carries `SmartMove` (`infantry.yaml:53`). So "only Force-Move works" is not a vague symptom — it localises the defect to the wrapper in one step, because the wrapper is *literally the only difference between the two code paths*. **Whenever a bug reproduces on Move and not on Force-Move, read `SmartMoveActivity` first and nothing else.**
- **Root cause: `ChooseArmamentsForTarget` filters on `IsTraitDisabled` only, and an empty armament is PAUSED, not disabled.** The literal `// FF TODO Check ammo?` at `AttackBase.cs:437` is not a nice-to-have — it is a live trap for every caller that reads "some weapon reaches this target" as "we can shoot it". `SmartMoveActivity` was such a caller (`:94`): a dry unit reported a weapon in range, cancelled its own move child (`:114`) and queued an attack (`:117`) that `AmmoPool.CannotFight` ended on its first tick (`Attack.cs:117`). `runningMoveActivity` stays `false`, so the move child is never re-queued (`:123` is skipped — a child *was* just queued) and the next tick re-scans with `ignoreScanInterval: true` and does it again. **Fixed point: the unit does not move one cell, so it never leaves the enemy's weapon range, so the interrupt never lifts.**
- **The freeze is invisible to every idle-triggered repair because the activity never completes.** `return TickChild(self) && runningMoveActivity` (`:132`) cannot be true while pinned, so `CurrentActivity != null` forever and `Actor.IsIdle` is false forever. This is the *third* instance of the shape `ed780538` named ("a man under orders is never idle, so nothing ever asked him again") and the first one that is not in the attack path at all. `AmmoPool`'s `INotifyBecomingIdle` handoff, `AutoSeekSupplies.INotifyIdle`, and AutoTarget's idle scan are all equally unreachable here.
- **The resupply errand pins itself by the same wrapper — the green line is drawn by an activity whose movement never runs.** `SeekSupplyProvider` calls `Mobile.MoveWithinRange` (`SeekSupplyProvider.cs:123`), which also goes through `WrapMove` (`Mobile.cs:677/683`). So the errand's own travel is a `SmartMoveActivity` and is pinned exactly like a player Move, while `SeekSupplyProvider.TargetLineNodes` (`:132-136`) keeps drawing the line to the truck. **"Order visibly issued, unit stationary" is the expected rendering of this bug, not evidence against it.**
- **Why the existing coverage could not see it: every prior scenario removed one of the two required ingredients.** The wedge needs a dry unit *and* an acquirable enemy inside weapon range *and* a move in flight. `test-queued-attackmove-survives-resupply` has the dry unit, the truck and the walk but **no enemy anywhere on its map** — so the scan returns Invalid, the move is queued normally, and it passes. `test-dry-inrange-idle-oscillation` has the dry unit and the in-range enemy but the unit is **stationary**, so no `SmartMoveActivity` exists to pin it; it measures 98% idle and passes. Neither is wrong; each is missing exactly the variable the other has. *General shape: when two green scenarios each omit a different one of a bug's preconditions, their greens do not compose into coverage of the conjunction.*
- **The fix reuses `AmmoPool.CannotFight` rather than adding a fourth ammo predicate, and the containment that buys is the point.** The set of units the resupply layer sends away (`AutoSeekSupplies.ReturnWhenEmpty`, `AmmoPool.AutoRearmIfAllEmpty`) is now *exactly* the set `SmartMoveActivity` refuses to pin. A unit cannot be simultaneously "too dry to be interrupted" and "not dry enough to be sent" — which is the failure mode `051d790a` documented when "empty" meant two different pool sets.
- **Still open, deliberately unfixed (see `bugs/discovered.md`): the same interrupt still stalls a PARTIALLY dry unit.** `CannotFight` requires every pool empty. A rifleman with an empty rifle and a loaded RPG facing infantry still returns the paused rifle from `ChooseArmamentsForTarget`, still cancels his move — and now the attack activity's guard does *not* fire (`CannotFight` is false), so he stops and aims instead of spinning. Milder, same family, needs its own measurement.

## 2026-08-11 — Transport doctrine recon: `@stable` lift is NOT permanently starved, `ForwardStaging` never touches a transport, the derrick ferry is already enabled on both profiles, and `Cargo.LockForPickup` destroys the player's queued transport orders

> **[promoted (one finding of six): → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise — **`Cargo.LockForPickup` silently cancels the transport's whole activity queue**, verified at source: `Passenger.Reserve` → `Cargo.ReserveSpace` (`Cargo.cs:371-396`) → `LockForPickup` (`:393`), whose body sets `state = Locked` and then calls `self.CancelActivity()` on the transport (`:412-419`). A passenger deciding to board therefore wipes a human player's shift-queue with no order issued and nothing logged — a genuine engine trap and the only finding here that is a fact about how the game works. **Rejected: the other five** — three are corrections to OTHER WORKSPACE documents (`recon/260808-transport-census.md` §0.3/§1.2 on `@stable` lift not being a permanent starve, and PIPELINE item 35's dependency on item 34), and those belong in the documents they correct, not in a reference doc; the `ForwardStaging`/drop-site-picker reads and the "`HeliDangerNav` already has every primitive" observation are design input for `plans/260811_transport_doctrine.md` and decay with it. Recording the split rather than the content so nobody re-promotes them: a correction to a tracker document is tracker work.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 43a08a1e).

Static read at `main @ 5eddff63` ahead of [`plans/260811_transport_doctrine.md`](plans/260811_transport_doctrine.md). Six findings; three of them **correct claims currently written down elsewhere in this repo**, which is why they are recorded rather than left in the plan.

- **CORRECTION to `recon/260808-transport-census.md` §0.3 (headline 5) and §1.2: `@stable` helicopter lift is not "a permanent starve".** The census reads `TransportMissionSlots: 0` on `@stable` as starving lift "to zero by construction". The gate is conditional: with the slot count at 0 the launcher falls through to `activeSquads.Count >= Info.MaxActiveSquads` (`HelicopterSquadBotModule.cs:1025-1026`; `MaxActiveSquads: 3` at `ai.yaml:1674`). A transport mission never increments `activeSquads`, so lift is blocked **only while three attack squads are live** — early game, and in any lull below three, `@stable` can and does launch lifts. **This inverts the `@stable` risk assessment for any transport work**: heli-transport changes are *not* inert on the benchmark control, they are intermittently live on it. Same shape as the standing `@stable` correction below — a fall-through branch is not a closed one.
- **`ForwardStaging` is attack-heli-only and cannot cause any transport behaviour.** `StageIdleHelicopters` filters on `AIHelicopterRole` and `continue`s unless the role is `AttackHeavy`/`AttackLight` (`:708-713`). It *is* genuinely danger-blind — `ForwardStagingCell` (`:737-751`) consults no field and the order is a bare `Move` (`:725`) — and it *is* set on `@stable` (`ai.yaml:1685-1687`), so it stays a real (and still live-unobserved) finding; it just belongs to the attack-heli file. **The actually danger-blind transport seam is `DispatchTransportDelivery` (`:1264-1291`)**: `Move` to the drop zone (`:1273`), queued `Unload` (`:1276`), queued `Move` home (`:1280`) — no field read on any leg. An aircraft `Move` is a straight line, so a lift flies the shortest path into the drop and back out again.
- **The drop-site picker cannot produce a safe landing site, and the reason is the candidate set, not the score.** `PickRiskWeightedDropZone` (`:1122-1179`) does read both danger channels (`:1144-1145`), but (a) it is an argmax with no floor (`:1153-1157`) — with every candidate lethal it returns the least-lethal lethal one, and (b) every candidate is an enemy-side cell: `{FindWeakestEnemyCell}` ∪ `{top N believed offensive POIs}` (`:1160-1176`). No candidate is a *safe cell near* an objective, so no re-weighting can yield an LZ short of one. **Non-obvious coupling:** making it a filter is not a local change — `EvaluateIdleTransport` omits the drop-zone precondition from its `launchable` proxy *specifically because* the picker is a weight and effectively never returns null (`:1571-1575`), so filtering re-opens the "Employ shadows Evacuate" pin that adversarial review of `fd3bc036` found. The two must move together.
- **`Cargo.LockForPickup` silently destroys the transport's queued orders — including a human player's shift-queue.** `Passenger.Reserve` → `Cargo.ReserveSpace` (`Cargo.cs:371-396`) calls `LockForPickup` (`:393`), which sets `state = Locked` (`:417`), **calls `self.CancelActivity()` on the transport** (`:419`), lands it if airborne (`:421-426`) and queues `WaitFor(state != Locked)` (`:428`); `ReleaseLock` fires only at `reservedWeight == 0` (`:405`) and restores nothing (`:431-443`). So the *first* soldier to reserve a seat wipes whatever the transport's owner had queued — on someone else's order. Same class as the shift-queued-order-breaks-ambush-hold defect: an unrelated mechanism discarding queued player intent. Consequence for PIPELINE item 34: "when all are done, it continues with its queue of orders" is **a repair, not an addition**.
- **PIPELINE item 35's hard dependency on item 34 does not hold as written.** The recorded reason is that "ferry the technician to the derrick" is a demand statement with "nowhere to be expressed until item 34's demand-publication layer exists". That channel exists and is enabled on **both** profiles: `UseTransportForDistantCaptures: true` / `TransportCaptureMinDistanceCells: 12` at `ai.yaml:186-187` (`@experimental.tecn`) and `:1893-1894` (`@stable.tecn`), routing `CaptureCoordinatorBotModule.TryFerryCapture` (`:1317-1331`) → `MountedTransportBotModule.TryReserveCaptureFerry` (`:249-284`), whose destination is `target.Location` — which the census itself calls "the **only** transport path in the codebase whose destination is a real objective handed in from outside" (census §1.3). So item 35 is diagnosis-and-tuning of a live path, not a new feature awaiting a layer. **And it is already diagnosable with no code change:** `CaptureCoordinatorBotModule.cs:1308-1309` logs `[exp-capture] issue … ferried=True|False` unconditionally (plain `Log.Write`, not behind `DebugLogging`) on every capture order, so one live match distinguishes "never attempted" from "attempted and refused". **Hazard to check when you do:** `transportModuleResolved` (`:1323-1328`) is a one-shot latch that caches the resolved module **including a `null` result** for the whole match — if the first capture is issued on a tick where the transport module is trait-disabled, the ferry is dead permanently. The enable conditions are paired (`ai.yaml:112`/`:1403`, `:1858`/`:1366`) so they *should* co-enable; the relative tick could not be established statically. NEEDS A LIVE LOOK — stated as a hazard, not a defect found.
- **Most actionable: `HeliDangerNav` already contains every primitive that transport route/landing safety needs, and the sampler is already built in the same file.** `PathMaxAirDanger` (`HeliDangerNav.cs:47-64`), `DetourWaypoint` (`:102-142`), `LeashedEngageCell` (`:71-95` — named for engagement, but it is literally "nearest cell to a target at or under a danger threshold", i.e. the safe-LZ search) and `SafestAirCellOnRing` (`:148-173`). All pure, integer-only, zero-RNG, NUnit-pinned. Consumers today are the attack squads (`HelicopterStates.cs:616`, `:619`, `:844`) and the careful-**scout** path (`HelicopterSquadBotModule.cs:967`); **grep confirms no transport path calls any of them.** The scout path is the template worth copying wholesale: same module, same fragile-airframe rationale (`ai.yaml:1761-1766`), sampler already bound at `:874`, and its gate `ReconSafetyMath.Acceptable(destAir, pathMax, threshold, distSq, capSq)` (`:1881-1894`) is a genuine three-part **filter** — exactly what the transport drop picker is not.
## 2026-08-11 — THE GROUND AND AIR DANGER REFERENCES DO NOT MOVE TOGETHER: one tuning change shifted ground −19.5% and air −43.9%. There is no single correction factor for the danger thresholds

> **[promoted (the rule, not the numbers): → influence-stack.md §Stage B — this EXTENDS the doc, which carried the 1000/5000 divisors and the 1.00x-1.28x band but said nothing about the two references responding differently. Mechanism verified first-hand: `ReferenceIntensity` medians over **only the contributing types** (`DangerFieldLayer.cs:228-243`, `if (kernel.Contributes)`) and the two channels draw from different populations (`WeaponThreatensAir` `:136-139` vs `WeaponThreatensGround` `:142-150`), so one shared tuning change re-medians two different sets. The code already states the consequence at `:391-395` (*"NOT interchangeable"*), which is the strongest form of the claim. Banked with the one property that IS statically derivable: the contributing population is invariant to the durability weight (`Compute` non-contributes only on `range/throughput/confidence <= 0`, `:157-158`; the weight enters at `:176`/`:192`). **Rejected: the six figures** — they are tool-run observations at two divisor settings, not re-derivable by reading code, and the pre-fix column would need the divisors reverted to reproduce.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 43a08a1e).

Measured on `auto/danger-durability` (base `f2a31035`) with `OpenRA.Utility ww3mod --danger-reference`, static, no game session. **Read this before re-deriving any threshold in danger units.** The `f2a31035` entry below measured only the ground channel and predicted −19.5%; that prediction was correct *and* insufficient.

| | before (`HealthDivisor` 10 / `CostDivisor` 50) | after (1000 / 5000) | shift |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ground reference** | 3412 | **2748** | **−19.5%** |
| **air reference** | 3627 | **2034** | **−43.9%** |
| ground spread (min/ref/max) | 164 / 3412 / 1,271,250 | 21 / 2748 / 245,000 | |
| air spread (min/ref/max) | — | 514 / 2034 / 76,890 | |
| contributing types | 92/424 ground | 92/424 ground, 44/424 air | unchanged |

- **Why they diverge.** `ReferenceIntensity` is a **median over the types that threaten that channel**, and the two channels are stamped from different populations — 92 ground-threatening types against 44 air-threatening ones. A change to the durability weight reweights each population around a *different* median type, so the two references move by unrelated amounts. Nothing about this is specific to the durability weight: **any** change to the kernel inputs (damage table, cadence model, weight, the contributing-population filter) will do the same.

- **The trap this sets.** The tempting shortcut after a rescale is "the reference moved −19.5%, so multiply every threshold by 1.24 and carry on". That is right for the ground consumers and **wrong by more than 2x for every air consumer** — `HelicopterSquadBotModule`'s AA leash and detour logic, and anything else converting through `AirDangerUnitsToField`. Air thresholds must be re-derived against the **air** reference, measured, never inferred from the ground one.

- **The two literal-zero thresholds are the exception and stay safe at any scale**, by construction: `AirDangerSafeThreshold: 0` and `GarrisonBotModule.MinBelievedDanger: 1` are scale-free presence tests (`DangerUnitsToField` maps 0 → 0 losslessly), which is exactly why they were left on the raw scale when the unit landed.

## 2026-08-11 — A test that TRANSCRIBES the default it is meant to protect passes against every change to that default. Proven, not argued: the old danger-kernel tests went green against a 100x divisor change

> **[promoted (as a caveat, since the defect is fixed): → influence-stack.md §Stage B. **FIXED-SINCE** at `f09183e2` — `DangerFieldKernelTest` now builds its params from `new DangerFieldLayerInfo()` and asserts against the live fields (`:26-33`), with the old `healthDivisor: 10, costDivisor: 50` transcript named in a comment, and it is a real pin: reverting `HealthDivisor` makes the rifleman weigh 122 instead of 100 and fails. **But it is only HALF fixed, and that residual is what got banked:** `RealHulls` still hardcodes HP/Cost/Throughput transcribed from the ruleset, so the test pins divisor *semantics* against a frozen ruleset snapshot — a mod-YAML HP change moves the real band while the test stays green. This is the knowledge-bank audit's Shape 4 ("NUnit-pinned where the test pins something weaker than the claim") instantiated, and the grep signature it names is the durable output.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 43a08a1e).

Found on `auto/danger-durability`. A defect **class**, not an instance — worth checking for wherever a pin is written against configured values.

- **The instance.** `DangerFieldKernelTest` built its `DangerKernelParams` from literals — `new(rangeBufferCells: 2, maxRadiusCells: 32, durabilityBase: 100, healthDivisor: 10, costDivisor: 50)` — described in a comment as "mirrors `DangerFieldLayerInfo` defaults". When `HealthDivisor` went 10 → 1000 and `CostDivisor` 50 → 5000, **the pre-change test file passed against the post-change engine: 1351 tests, 0 failures.** Verified directly by stashing only the test file and re-running. The tests were pinning their own transcript, not the shipped configuration, and had been doing so ever since the ruleset outgrew the RA-era values.

- **Why this is worse than an ordinary stale test.** It fails *silently and in the safe-looking direction*. A drifted assertion normally goes **red** and demands attention; a transcribed default goes **green** and actively certifies the thing it no longer describes. It also survives review, because the literal sits next to a comment truthfully stating what it was copied from — the comment is evidence of provenance, not of currency.

- **The fix, and the rule.** Construct the shipping Info and read the fields off it: `static readonly DangerFieldLayerInfo Shipping = new(); … new DangerKernelParams(Shipping.RangeBufferCells, …, Shipping.HealthDivisor, Shipping.CostDivisor)`. Then a retune **moves the test** instead of leaving it green against numbers nothing uses. The same discipline was already in this file for `new SupplyFollowerBotModuleInfo().EvacDangerUnits` — so the pattern was present and simply not applied to the kernel params. **Detector (grep signature): a test constructing a `*Params`/`*Info`-shaped value from integer literals, with a comment saying "mirrors"/"matches"/"same as" some `Info`.** If the value is meant to track a default, it must be *read* from the default.

- **Corollary for behavioural pins.** The same file already carried the sharper form of this lesson from an earlier round — fixtures were once hard-coded to the *broken* formula's outputs and would have gone green forever. Both are the same failure: **a test whose fixtures are copies rather than computations documents the state of the world when it was written, and nothing after.**

## 2026-08-11 — An OMITTED armor class in a `Versus` table is FULL damage, not zero — so the danger field's "phantom weapons" are real threats and the `min=164` floor was never a phantom

> **[promoted: → conventions.md §`Versus`: an OMITTED armor class is FULL damage. Re-verified line by line in `DamageWarhead.DamageVersus` (`Warheads/DamageWarhead.cs:96-110`): `damage = 100`, empty-`Versus` early return (`:101-102`), and the `Versus.ContainsKey(a.Info.Type)` filter (`:105`) that makes an unlisted class take the unmodified 100%. All three fail-open shapes are visible in that one predicate (null `Type`, `IsTraitDisabled` conditional `Armor`, non-empty `HitShapeInfo.ArmorTypes`). The mod's armor population re-derived independently and matches the entry exactly — nine classes, **`Brick` is not one of them**, and `Kevlar` sits on `^Soldier` (`infantry.yaml:173-174`) while non-`^Soldier` actors keep `^Infantry`'s `None` (`:34-35`), which is precisely what makes the omission selective enough to survive eyeballing. `DumpDangerReferenceCommand.cs` and `RulesetArmorTypes`/`WarheadIsHarmless` both present. The durability-band figures agree with what is already in influence-stack.md §Stage B, so nothing there needed correcting.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ dc8e0abf).

Verified on `auto/danger-durability` (base `f2a31035`), entirely statically. **Supersedes the last bullet of the entry below** (the "bonus defect" claim that `WeaponThroughput` ignoring `Versus` was crediting non-threats). The reference numbers this produced are in the ground/air entry above.

- **The re-derivation is now a shipped command, and it is validated against the live log rather than merely plausible.** `OpenRA.Utility ww3mod --danger-reference` (`UtilityCommands/DumpDangerReferenceCommand.cs`) runs the production `ExtractKernelFacts` / `ReferenceIntensity` over the default ruleset. Flipping `HealthDivisor`/`CostDivisor` back to their RA values and re-running reproduces the 2026-08-10 play log **digit for digit** — `ground=3412 air=3627 ground-types=92/424 min=164 max=1271250` — which is what licenses trusting the post-change numbers from the same tool. The previous entry proved this was *possible* with a scratch parser; this makes it repeatable by anyone, and it now also prints the air spread, the per-warhead harmless verdict, the live durability band, and `worst-first-multiply` (the overflow-headroom claim in `Compute`'s comment, checked against the ruleset it is a claim about).

- **CORRECTION: `IskanderTargeter`/`HIMARSTargeter` are NOT harmless, and excluding "phantom weapons" removes nothing from this ruleset.** The entry below reported them as non-threats padding the contributing population, on the strength of a `Versus` block that zeroes `None, Wood, Concrete, Light, Medium, Heavy, Brick`. Two things are wrong with reading that as harmless. `Brick` **is not an armor class in WW3MOD at all** (the nine are `Concrete, Heavy, Indestructable, Kevlar, Light, Medium, None, Unarmored, Wood`), and `Kevlar` — `^Soldier`'s armor, reaching **14 infantry templates** via `^CamoSoldier` (`^AR ^SN ^AT ^AA ^E1–^E4 ^E6 ^MT ^TL ^MEDI ^AmphibiousSoldier ^PILOT`, of which only `^PILOT` reverts to `None`), i.e. effectively the whole combat-infantry roster — together with `Unarmored` and `Indestructable` are simply **unlisted**. So both targeters deal their full 50 to all of them. (Non-`^Soldier` actors keep `^Infantry`'s `Type: None`, which the table *does* zero — so the bug is selective, which is exactly why eyeballing the table missed it.) The contributing population is unchanged at 92/424, and `min` fell 164 → 21 purely from the weight rescale, not from any exclusion.

- **THE RULE, and it is the generalisable half: in `DamageWarhead.DamageVersus`, omission is the OPPOSITE of a zero.** An **empty** `Versus` early-returns full damage (`DamageWarhead.cs:101-102`); a **non-empty** one filters to the classes it *lists* (`:105`), so an unlisted class matches nothing, `ApplyPercentageModifiers` runs over an empty sequence, and the victim takes the unmodified **100%**. A table that zeroes six classes and omits a seventh is a *full-damage* weapon against the seventh, not a weak one. Any "this weapon cannot hurt anything" judgement must therefore be made against **the ruleset's armor population**, never against the table alone — and three further shapes make it unprovable outright, because each ends with the same empty filter: a null `ArmorInfo.Type`, a **conditional** `Armor` (it is a `ConditionalTraitInfo`, so it can be absent at runtime), and a non-empty `HitShapeInfo.ArmorTypes`. `DangerFieldLayer.RulesetArmorTypes`/`WarheadIsHarmless` implement exactly this and fail open on all of them; NUnit-pinned in `DangerFieldKernelTest`.

- **The weight is now a tie-break, and the honest way to state that is a BOUND, not "it never re-ranks".** Band 1.20x–29.50x (median 1.25x) → **1.00x–1.28x (median 1.00x)**. A multiplicative weight can only invert two types whose throughputs sit within its own max/min ratio: that ratio was **24.6x** — wider than most of the ruleset's throughput spread, so the "weight" was a second, HP-shaped lethality term — and is now **1.28x**. Note the cost term is nearly inert at `CostDivisor: 5000` (only ≥$5,000 units contribute at all, at most +1 point); the health term carries essentially the whole signal. Worth knowing before anyone tunes this again.

- **The NUnit suite was structurally incapable of catching the divisor error** — `DangerFieldKernelTest` transcribed the Info defaults instead of reading them, so the pre-change tests pass against the post-change engine. Written up as its own defect *class* in the transcribed-defaults entry above.

## 2026-08-11 — The `[danger] reference` line is reproducible STATICALLY from YAML — no build, no run. And doing so confirms the durability weight is RA-scaled, but shows the fix moves the reference by only −19%

> **[rejected: **PARTLY-WRONG as stated, and its substance is already in the doc correctly worded.** "No build" is false for the shipped route — `--danger-reference` is a C# utility command (`UtilityCommands/DumpDangerReferenceCommand.cs`, header shows `dotnet engine/bin/OpenRA.Utility.dll`); the no-build claim belonged to a scratch offline MiniYaml parser the entry itself flags as not committed, and it is not in the tree. influence-stack.md already says *"re-derivable statically with `OpenRA.Utility ww3mod --danger-reference` (no game session)"*, which is the accurate form — **no game session, no map, no RNG; a build is required.** Confirmed the command calls PRODUCTION code rather than a reimplementation (`RulesetArmorTypes`, `ExtractKernelFacts`, `ReferenceIntensity`, `Compute`).
